business: yerby, a cold-brewed sparkling yerba mate drink in a 330 ml can, launching in Czechia
by_segment: Active health-focused adult (sport most weeks, eats clean)
why_not: 55 CZK for one can is too much when I'm on a starter salary and I already grab mate or a pre-workout for less on Rohlík or GymBeam. Clean ingredients are nice, but every brand says natural now.

I drink a can around training three times a week, and from GymBeam or Vilgain I get energy cans for around 25 to 35 crowns, often in a multipack deal. 55 a can for something I expect to taste like grassy tea is too much to switch to on my wage.

I grab my energy drink at the petrol station or Albert on the way, and this is only online or in cafés I don't stop at while driving. The cleaner ingredients appeal to me, but I'm not ordering cans to my house for something I've never tasted and suspect tastes like grass tea.

It sounds like exactly the kind of can I'd try and post, but I'm not ordering drinks from some e-shop, and 'selected cafés' tells me nothing about whether I'll ever see it. If it's not on Rohlík or in a fridge I walk past, it just won't happen this month.

I've drunk the same energy drink for years and I know exactly how it hits when I'm cramming at 1am. I'm not going to gamble an exam night on a yerba mate with 80 mg that might feel weaker, and I'm not ordering cans from an e-shop when my usual is at every corner shop.

Before a ride I have coffee at home, and on the trail I drink water from my bottle. A fizzy can doesn't fit into either, and I'm not ordering from some separate e-shop when my groceries already come from Rohlík.
Before training I want a proper kick, and 80 mg is less than my usual can or a scoop of pre-workout. At 55 CZK a can that's more money for less effect, so I'd just keep ordering from GymBeam.
On a night or early shift I need something that actually keeps me up, and 80 mg is less than the Monster I usually grab. Paying 55 CZK for less kick than my normal can doesn't make sense to me.

Unsweetened yerba mate sounds like bitter grass tea to me, and I'm not paying 55 crowns to find out when I get pre-workout or energy cans from GymBeam for much less. 80 mg of caffeine isn't more kick than what I already drink before training.

Fruit concentrate means sugar, and the pitch never says how many grams per can, so as someone who only drinks Zero versions I'm not ordering it blind. And if I want a mate, YEAHRBA is already in my Rohlík basket for less.
why_yes: I already only drink Zero versions and read every label, so a can with just water, mate and fruit concentrate and no sweeteners at all is exactly what I look for. 55 CZK doesn't matter to me, so I'd grab one at a café and order a few for exam nights if the taste works.

The label is exactly what I look for: water, yerba mate and fruit concentrate, no sweeteners or additives, so I'd try a can or two when I see it in a café. But I'm not ordering it from a separate e-shop when matcha at home costs me a fraction of that.

If it's in the fridge at the bistro where I eat lunch, a clean yerba mate with just three ingredients beats a Monster for me, and 55 CZK is normal café money. I'd grab one or two to try, but I won't order cans from an e-shop and it isn't at the petrol stations where I actually stop most.

The label is honestly the cleanest I've seen on a caffeinated can: water, mate, fruit concentrate, done. I'd grab one or two in a café to swap for the energy drink I keep next to me during exam prep, but I'm not committing to a habit yet.

A sparkling cold-brewed mate in a slim can is exactly the kind of new thing I grab from a café fridge to try and post, so I'd buy one out of curiosity and maybe a second if it actually tastes good. Past that, it has to beat my usual coffee or matcha, and I'm not sure it will.
